title: Top Air Fryers for Fast Weeknight Dinners (2026)
summary: The Ninja Air Fryer Pro is the best pick for most people, with the COSORI TurboBlaze for crispiness and the Philips 3000 for family dual-basket cooking.
method: Picks come from Tom's Guide (updated Jun 2, 2026) and RTINGS (best air fryers updated Aug 21, 2026 and best 4-quart updated Aug 27, 2026). Every model listed was tested by both outlets.
assumptions: Prices change often, so we quote a price only where Tom's Guide's price widget or text shows one, and label it. Wirecutter's and Serious Eats's picks were not available to us in full, so they are not used here.

products.name: Ninja Air Fryer Pro 4-in-1 (AF141)
why: Tom's Guide names the Ninja Air Fryer Pro 4-in-1 its best air fryer for most people. The five-quart basket handled meal prep for four, french fries crisped in under 10 minutes, and the nonstick, dishwasher-safe basket cleaned up easily. A lift-out insert lets you cook straight on the base for saucier food.

RTINGS picks the same machine as its best 4-quart air fryer, and in its head-to-head test it makes much better-quality fried food than the Ninja Crispi. It also allows fully manual settings and a low minimum temperature for dehydrating or proofing dough.

Temperature range 100 to 400°F (Tom's Guide)

products.name: COSORI TurboBlaze Air Fryer
why: RTINGS names the COSORI TurboBlaze its best air fryer for most people, calling it an easy pick if you want reliably crispy snacks.
Tom's Guide rates it four stars and says it looks a lot like Ninja's machines, but its prices have crept up, so it is no longer an obvious budget pick. Wait for a sale before buying.

products.name: Philips 3000 Series Dual Basket Air Fryer
why: Tom's Guide calls the Philips 3000 its favorite dual-zone air fryer, one it would trust with expensive cuts of meat. The sensitive temperature controls do a great job rendering fat from bacon and wings and keep salmon tender, and the vortex base browns potato wedges evenly.
The two drawers are different sizes, so you can use the small one for a single serving and the large one for family meals. RTINGS has also tested this model.

Vortex base circulates air; dishwasher-safe parts
Tom's Guide's price widget showed $210.38 (list $249.99); check the current price
pros: Evenly cooks thanks to the vortex base
cons: You cannot cook flat on the basket base (Tom's Guide)

products.skip_if: You have limited counter space or a small household

products.name: Dreo ChefMaker Combi Fryer
why: Tom's Guide calls the Dreo ChefMaker an air fryer that is actually smart. A temperature probe tells the machine when food is done, and it won a Tom's Guide Award in 2024 as the most exciting air fryer release of the year. One tester got medium-rare steaks to an astonishing degree of accuracy and gave it a rare 4.5-star review.
It also adds a steam feature for baking and toasting. The guide's managing editor has used one in her own kitchen for years. RTINGS has also tested it.

products.name: Ninja Crispi
why: Tom's Guide picks the Crispi as the best small air fryer, though it admits it is not really an air fryer in the usual sense. A lid with four presets sits on glass containers you can also use for meal prep, fridge storage and travel, so it suits students, small kitchens and RVs.
RTINGS tested it directly against the Ninja Pro and found the Pro makes much better-quality fried food and is more versatile, with manual settings and a lower minimum temperature.

Four presets, 158 to 350°F range (Tom's Guide)
Glass cooking containers; you can see food as it cooks
Tom's Guide's price widget showed $49.99; check the current price

cons: Less crispy than the Ninja Pro in RTINGS's test
products.best_for: Singles, students and anyone short on counter space

products.name: COSORI Iconic Air Fryer
why: Tom's Guide picks the Iconic as its best PFAS-free air fryer: a stainless steel machine with a DC motor that cooks fast and evenly, and a five-year warranty that is unusual for air fryers. The tester found cleanup easy and results consistently crisp for chicken, fries and vegetables.
Tom's Guide says nonstick coatings are highly unlikely to be toxic, but if you would still prefer to avoid them, this is the pick. RTINGS has also tested it.

tips.title: How to choose
items: Tom's Guide says the quart rating is fairly meaningless; a wide, shallow basket that lets food lie flat gives better results than a tall narrow one.
More power means faster, crispier food, and Tom's Guide finds anything under about $50 tends to struggle.
Preset modes only choose a time and temperature, so they make no difference to how the food cooks.
Skip toaster-oven styles unless you need one.
Tom's Guide finds them clunkier to clean and use than a basket air fryer.

faq: Tom's Guide says it is highly unlikely they are toxic and that PFAS does not automatically mean toxic. If you would still prefer to avoid nonstick, the COSORI Iconic is its PFAS-free pick.
Which air fryer is best for a family?
The Philips 3000 Dual Basket for cooking two foods at once, or the Ninja Pro XL if you prefer one large basket.
Is the Ninja Crispi a real air fryer?
Tom's Guide says it is not really one: it has four presets and no temperature control, and RTINGS found the Ninja Pro cooks better. It is best for small kitchens.
